verdict.headline: Consistent with selection bias
verdict.detail: The winning Sharpe is no better than what searching this many parameter combinations would produce from noise. Do not allocate to it.

warnings: Seeded demo run — computed ahead of time from committed, recorded BTCUSDT bars so the first paint shows real numbers. The live sweep replaces it automatically.

verdict.headline: The winner sits on a slope
verdict.detail: Neighbouring combinations retain 44% of the winner's Sharpe on average (0.68 against 1.52). Degrading, but not collapsing — treat the reported parameters as the top of a ridge rather than a stable operating point.

verdict.headline: The edge does not survive the fold boundary
verdict.detail: Only 1 of 4 folds were profitable out-of-sample, at a median efficiency of -0.26. Parameters selected on one window stop working on the next, which is the definition of overfitting.

descriptions: Buy and hold the instrument. A high loading means the strategy is mostly directional exposure.
Long after a positive trailing 30-bar return, short after a negative one. A high loading means the edge is generic trend-following.
Long while trailing 30-bar volatility is below its expanding average, short above. The threshold uses only prior bars, so the factor is implementable rather than built with hindsight.
factors.note: Time-series factors built from this instrument's own bars — not Fama-French and not cross-sectional, which one symbol cannot produce. t-statistics are plain OLS; a Newey-West correction would widen them, so the significance shown here is generous.

checks.label: Deflated Sharpe
checks.why: Prices the search itself: the probability the edge is real after paying for how many combinations were tried.

checks.label: Walk-forward OOS Sharpe
checks.why: Measured on data the parameters never saw. In-sample results are a fit; this is a test.

checks.label: Walk-forward efficiency
checks.why: How much of the in-sample edge survives out-of-sample. Below half means the backtest is mostly fitting.

checks.label: Parameter neighbourhood
checks.why: A real edge degrades smoothly as parameters move. An isolated spike is a coordinate found in noise.

checks.label: Alpha t-statistic
checks.why: Return not explained by market, trend or volatility exposure — otherwise it is a factor bet in disguise.

checks.label: Trade count
checks.why: Below about thirty trades the Sharpe is dominated by a handful of outcomes and its confidence interval spans zero.

regimes.note: Trend = close vs its 200-bar SMA with a ±2% deadband; SMA warm-up bars are unclassified. The volatility split uses the full-sample median — hindsight, so it describes where returns came from and is not a tradable signal. Per-regime drawdown compounds only that regime's bars stitched together: a diagnostic, not a drawdown anyone lived through.
